Name: John Calvin
Summary: French reformer whose Institutes became Protestantism's most influential systematic theology. From Geneva he trained pastors, shaped Reformed worship, and stressed God's sovereignty and the authority of Scripture.
Contribution: Systematized Reformed theology, modeled disciplined church life, and spread the Reformation through trained ministers.
KeyWorks: Institutes of the Christian Religion; Commentaries on Scripture
Testimony: A shy scholar who never sought fame, Calvin's life testified to a single aim: that God be glorified in church, city, and home.
